headline: Westerlo's hot run meets a market that keeps it close
summary: Westerlo have won 4 straight league games, scoring 15 and conceding 3, and at home to Antwerp they made 2.43 expected goals in a 5-1 win. Beveren's away day is the contrast: they lost at Kortrijk with just 0.42 expected goals, though they arrive after a 3-0 cup win with Ferre Slegers on the scoresheet. Across six bookmakers, margin removed, Westerlo are 46% favourites, Beveren 28.7% and the draw 25.3%. The goal line is 3.25, with over at 47.9% — fewer than half expect it. The read: form points one way, the market still keeps this close.
read: Westerlo are the form team of this fixture — five straight wins, 17 goals scored and only three conceded — and the market makes them 46% favourites at home against a Beveren side sitting 11th. The goals line sits at 3.17 with over 3.25 nearly a coin flip, so the expectation is an open game rather than a controlled one.

facts.fact: Westerlo are 46.0% favourites to win this, more than one and a half times Beveren's 28.7%.
facts.meaning: The market makes the home side clear favourites, but not overwhelming ones — the draw takes a quarter of the probability.

facts.fact: Westerlo have won their last five matches in all competitions by a combined 17 goals to 3.
facts.meaning: They come into this as the form side of the fixture, scoring heavily and conceding little.

facts.fact: Westerlo's 5-1 win over Antwerp on 11 October came with 2.43 xG to Antwerp's 0.91.
facts.meaning: The scoreline reflected the chances created — this is a side generating quality, not riding deflections.

facts.fact: Westerlo are 6th in the Jupiler Pro League after eight games; Beveren are 11th.
facts.meaning: A mid-table gap of five places separates the sides going into the weekend.

facts.fact: The market's fair goal total is 3.17, with the main line at 3.25 and over priced at 47.9%.
facts.meaning: This is expected to be an open game, with the market split almost evenly on whether it clears three goals.

facts.fact: The handicap fair line is -0.36, with the main line at -0.25.
Beveren lost 0-1 at Kortrijk on 20 September having created just 0.42 xG.
facts.meaning: Their away attacking output has been the weak point, and this trip is to the league's in-form attack.

facts.fact: Ferre Slegers scored one and assisted another in Beveren's 3-0 Croky Cup win over Habay-la-Neuve.
facts.meaning: Beveren come into this off a comfortable cup win with fringe players stating a case for league minutes.

sources.fact: Westerlo beat Patro Eisden 2-0 in the Croky Cup, with goals from Cisse Sandra and Saito, and goalkeeper Jungdal also played a key role in the qualification.
Westerlo go into the Beveren match on four consecutive league wins and can make it five in a row, a run of fifteen points out of fifteen.
Westerlo coach Issame Charaï says he does not want to focus on the statistics of a possible fifth straight league win.
Westerlo coach Issame Charaï continues to keep faith in striker Tsimba despite his missed chances against Patro Eisden.
Westerlo are drawn away to Union Saint-Gilloise in the last 16 of the Croky Cup.
Beveren beat amateurs Habay-la-Neuve 3-0 in the Croky Cup, with Ferre Slegers scoring one and assisting another, while Arno Verschueren and Viktor Olatunji scored their first goals for the club.
Beveren's coach said his side would make at least five changes for the cup tie against Habay-la-Neuve, partly out of necessity.
Ferre Slegers said after the Habay-la-Neuve cup win: "I wanted to prove myself."
